title: Preserve original runtime ACL atomically before concurrent projection migrations

incident_context.root_cause: bootstrap_schema committed _reconcile_runtime_ddl in the initial transaction, but _apply_grants was guarded by 'not concurrent_files' and deferred to the end of the concurrent autocommit phase. When concurrent/autocommit phase failures occurred before deferred grants, ownership remained transferred to the migration authority while runtime role grants were never executed, causing runtime SELECT true before -> false after.

operations: _reconcile_runtime_ddl: alters schema/table ownership of known projection tables from runtime to migration authority and revokes CREATE/TRIGGER
_apply_grants: verifies runtime holds no DDL authority, grants schema USAGE, and grants SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on existing PROJECTION_TABLES
phase_1_transactional_authority_and_acl.atomicity_and_failure_semantics: Authority reconciliation, transactional DDL, and complete runtime ACL restoration settle atomically in a single transaction. If any failure occurs during this phase (including partial grant failure), the entire transaction rolls back, restoring original table/schema ownership and prior runtime permissions.

operations: REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY for any invalid indexes (indisvalid=false)
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS across concurrent migration files (002_add_trade_journey_search_indexes.sql)
phase_2_nontransactional_concurrent_inde.atomicity_and_failure_semantics: PostgreSQL requires concurrent indexes to execute outside transaction blocks. Because Phase 1 already committed complete runtime ACLs (USAGE + SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), any subsequent concurrent index failure leaves the existing BFF runtime operational and able to read and write without losing table access.

acceptance_verification.ac1_atomic_authority_and_acl_settlement: Verified: authority reconciliation (_reconcile_runtime_ddl), transactional DDL (tx_files), and complete runtime ACL restoration (_apply_grants) commit atomically in Phase 1 before opening the autocommit concurrent connection.
acceptance_verification.ac2_concurrent_and_partial_grant_failure: Verified: test_bootstrap_schema_concurrent_failure_preserves_runtime_dml_and_usage_seven_tables proves runtime SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and schema USAGE are preserved after concurrent phase failure; test_bootstrap_schema_partial_grant_failure_rolls_back_authority_and_acl_seven_tables proves partial grant failure rolls back authority reconciliation and table ownership.
acceptance_verification.ac3_boundaries_and_limits_retained: Verified: runtime nonadmin checks, runtime no-DDL boundary enforcement, known schema/object/owner checks, configurable bounded migration timeouts (300s/30s), concurrent index execution, invalid-index repair, and idempotent re-execution are strictly retained.
acceptance_verification.ac4_owned_real_postgresql_tests: Verified: 12 tests in test_journey_search_migration.py pass against owned real PostgreSQL 16 (docker container on 127.0.0.1:15432) with separate nonadmin runtime and migration roles and complete 7-table schema, and test_bootstrap_schema_concurrent_failure_minimal_controller_preserves_runtime proves minimal-controller fixture remains fail-safe. No tests skipped.
acceptance_verification.ac5_evidence_separation: Verified: evidence JSON accurately details the atomic transactional authority/ACL phase vs the nontransactional concurrent index phase.
acceptance_verification.ac6_hosted_and_l1_l12_obligations: Full L1-L12 natural hosted authenticated browser restart and exact rollback obligations remain unaccepted until genuine hosted proofs are produced.
